summary: This informational RFC describes the role and responsibilities of the Independent Submission Editor (ISE), who approves documents in the Independent Submission stream, working with editors and reviewers and the RFC Production Center. It was replaced by RFC 8730.

plainLanguage.summary: Some RFCs come from outside the usual groups. This describes the person who decides which ones are accepted. A newer RFC 8730 replaced it.

subtitle: The role and responsibilities of the Independent Submission Editor for RFCs

tldr.problem: The RFC series includes documents from multiple submission streams (IETF, IRTF, and Independent), each with different approval processes. The Independent Submission stream needs its own senior editor role to maintain quality and manage submissions outside the formal working group structures.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6548 defines the Independent Submission Editor (ISE) position: a senior technical individual appointed by the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) who reviews and approves Independent Submissions, maintains technical quality, coordinates with the RFC Production Center, and interacts with both the RSE and IAOC.
tldr.outcome: The ISE role provides a clear governance structure for independent submissions, ensuring they meet quality standards while preserving the RFC series' openness to diverse contributions from outside traditional working groups.

today: RFC 6548 was replaced by RFC 8730 in May 2020. The role of ISE continues to provide oversight of independent submissions to the RFC series.

sections.title: Purpose and Authority
sections.content: RFC 6548 describes the function and responsibilities of the RFC Independent Submission Editor (ISE). The Independent Submission stream is one of several streams that produce draft RFCs, with the ISE as its approver. The ISE is overall responsible for activities within the Independent Submission stream, working with draft editors and reviewers, and interacting with the RFC Production Center, RFC Series Editor (RSE), and the Internet Architecture Board (IAB). Unlike the IETF or IRTF streams, the Independent Submission stream and its ISE are not under the authority of the RSE or the RFC Series Oversight Committee (RSOC).
sections.plainLanguage: The ISE is the chief decision-maker for RFCs submitted outside the IETF. They report to the IAB instead of to the RFC editor.

sections.title: Qualifications and Selection
sections.content: The ISE is a senior position requiring broad technical competence across internet technologies, thorough familiarity with the RFC series, ability to define advisory and review arrangements, good standing in the technical community, excellent English and editorial skills, and the ability to work effectively in a multi-actor environment with divided authority. These qualifications are desired, not absolute requirements. The individual is selected by the IAB after collecting community input, using an approach similar to that used for selecting IAOC members: the ISE is considered a volunteer function, though the IAB deems maintaining the Independent Submission stream part of its supported activities.
sections.plainLanguage: The ISE must understand protocols well, know the RFC series, write clearly, and be respected in the technical community. The IAB picks the ISE after asking for community suggestions.

sections.title: Responsibilities and Support
sections.content: The ISE is responsible for maintaining technical quality of the Independent Submission stream, reviewing, approving and processing Independent Submissions, forwarding approved draft RFCs to the RFC Production Center, defining and developing the scope of the stream, reviewing and approving errata for Independent Submissions, and coordinating with IAB and RSE on RFC Series policies. The ISE may select individuals for an Advisory Board to assist on special topics, and may have assistants. The ISE is supported by an Independent Submission Editorial Board, which is a volunteer board existing at the ISE's pleasure. The IAOC includes ISE-related costs in its budget as part of IAB-supported activities.
sections.plainLanguage: The ISE reviews submissions, decides which to approve, checks fixes to old RFCs, and keeps the submission process fair and transparent.
